finding: The FinCEN analysis looks only at (ff)(5)(i)(A), 'acceptance ... and transmission'. It leaves out (ff)(5)(i)(B), 'Any other person engaged in the transfer of funds'. That clause is the one most likely to reach a platform that originates or transmits payment instructions and files (F7 transmission to the ODFI, F9 partner API instructions). The executive findings then state the acceptance-only reading as fact. The (ii)(A) exclusion is also over-read: it covers delivery, communication or network-access services 'used by a money transmitter', so it does not cover instruction-only services in general.
evidence: Executive findings §2 item 3: 'Under FinCEN's definition, money transmission begins with *acceptance* of funds, which the design avoids' (no [AS] label). Financial review §2.1: 'the definition's first element ("acceptance") is not met. The exclusions are therefore not needed'; CQ-1: '(ii)(A) supports instruction-only service'. 31 CFR 1010.100(ff)(5)(i)(B) (LII https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/31/1010.100, read 2026-11-25): 'Any other person engaged in the transfer of funds.' (ii)(A): 'Provides the delivery, communication, or network access services used by a money transmitter'.
recommended_fix: Quote (i)(B) in financial review §2.1 and add it to CQ-1 and CQ-2. Relabel the executive-findings sentence as a proposed interpretation [AS] pending counsel. Limit the (ii)(A) claim to services provided to a party that is itself a money transmitter (for example the ODFI or partner).

finding: The justification misstates IRC 170(f)(8). The substantiation burden falls on the donor, who must obtain a contemporaneous written acknowledgment (CWA); the donee has no 170(f)(8) obligation. The donee-side legal duties are 170(f)(18) (DAF CWA content) and IRC 6115 quid-pro-quo disclosure, penalized under 6714. Neither is cited.
evidence: BR-FIN-013 justification: 'IRC 170(f)(8) acknowledgment obligations fall on the sponsor; platform supports them.' The financial review §2.7 states it correctly: '170(f)(8) denies a deduction ... without a contemporaneous written acknowledgment' (that is, the donor's deduction).
recommended_fix: Reword: the donor's deduction depends on a CWA that the sponsor issues; 170(f)(18) prescribes the DAF CWA content; 6115 and 6714 apply to quid-pro-quo contributions over USD 75. Keep the basis conditional-legal, but cite 170(f)(18) and 6115.

finding: The justification attributes the IRC 4967 tax to the sponsor. 4966 taxes the sponsoring organization and agreeing fund managers. 4967 taxes the donor, advisor or related person who advises and receives a more-than-incidental benefit, and agreeing fund managers, not the sponsor.
evidence: BR-FIN-014 justification: 'IRC 4966/4967 taxable distribution risk falls on sponsor; platform enforces sponsor policy.'
recommended_fix: Split the statement: 4966 falls on the sponsor and fund managers; 4967 falls on donors, advisors and fund managers. The prohibited-benefit check protects donors and advisors as well as the sponsor.

finding: OFAC coverage stops at screening. Neither the baseline nor the review names the OFAC reporting duties for blocked property and rejected transactions (31 CFR 501.603 and 501.604, generally within 10 business days) or the recordkeeping duty (501.601). Those dates must be in the obligation register even if the sponsor files the reports. 'conditional-legal' also understates the basis: OFAC prohibitions bind every U.S. person, including Echelon, without any applicability condition.
evidence: BR-FIN-022: 'blocking and rejection are human decisions'; it names no reporting deadline or record. A search of the repository for 501.603, 501.604 or 'rejected transaction' returns nothing. Financial review §2.6 cites only the 2019 Framework (SRC-FIN2-009) and daf-landscape's '10-year records ... not re-verified'.
recommended_fix: Add the reporting and recordkeeping obligations (verified against eCFR 31 CFR Part 501 Subpart C) to BR-GOV-009 and BR-FIN-022, with an owner (sponsor or Echelon per CQ-7). Record the prohibition as basis 'legal' and the screening method as framework-selected.

finding: The Nacha role and fraud-monitoring statements carry evidence class [A], but the review admits it never read the Rules (only Nacha summary pages). Bank question B2 asks 'at what volume' fraud-monitoring duties apply, although by the review's own dates both phases took effect before 2026-11-25. BR-FIN-019 is basis framework-selected and does not cite the Nacha fraud-monitoring obligation that a TPSP takes on through its ODFI or originator agreement.
evidence: Review §2.3: '[A, network rules, SRC-FIN2-004]' and 'Rules effective 2026-03-20 (Phase 1) and 2026-06-22 practical date (Phase 2)'. §6 Limits: 'The Nacha Operating Rules text ... were not read.' The source register says SRC-FIN2-004 and -010 are 'Summary page, not Rules text'.
recommended_fix: Downgrade these statements to industry-body summary [IC] until the Rules are read. Update B2 to ask which obligations now apply (not 'at what volume'), after verifying the current Phase 2 scope. Give BR-FIN-019 a contractual or conditional-legal Nacha basis.

finding: The artifacts disagree on which questions block requirements finalization. The financial review says counsel questions and the entity map block it. The registers and executive findings say only 8 owner-only items do, so the owner could finalize the baseline (ODP-01) without counsel input on the funds-flow perimeter.
evidence: Financial review §5: 'Before requirements finalization: CQ-1, CQ-3, CQ-5, CQ-6 and CQ-10; entity map (fact 1)'. question-dispositions.csv: OQ-102, OQ-216, OQ-205 and OQ-756 are 'dependent-legal, production-launch'. Executive findings §2 item 8: 'Only 8 block requirements finalization, and all 8 are owner decisions that need no paid advice.' Counsel doc §1: 'Requirements are not blocked'.
recommended_fix: Re-tier OQ-102, OQ-216, OQ-205 and OQ-756 (and the CQ items) as requirements-finalization, or state explicitly that BR-FIN-020 and BR-FIN-006 wording is provisional pending CQ-1, 3, 5, 6 and 10. Correct executive findings item 8 and the ODP-01 scope.

finding: Unbound holds sponsor-delegated credentials that send irreversible instructions: F7 file transmission to the ODFI and F9 partner API calls. The only check that an instruction is 'sponsor-authorized' is Unbound's own release worker reading Unbound's own database. A compromised Unbound or a privileged Echelon administrator (the owner, who per BR-FIN-002 can write the database) can therefore dispatch payments. BR-FIN-006 does_not_prevent omits this path. BR-FIN-020's test ('able unilaterally to execute') passes only because Unbound defines 'execute' to exclude relaying under delegation.
evidence: BR-FIN-006 does_not_prevent: 'Fraud by a legitimately authorized sponsor user; social engineering of approvers.' BR-FIN-002 does_not_prevent: 'Administrator or migration-role writes'. Financial review F9: 'Unbound sends instruction to partner API'; CQ-4: 'Would transmitting files directly to the ODFI change status?'. Unbound CNV-LEG-001: "relaying a sponsor-authorised instruction under the sponsor's delegation is permitted and is not execution by Unbound."
recommended_fix: Add the Echelon-admin or compromised-Unbound dispatch path to BR-FIN-006 does_not_prevent and residual_risk. Require sponsor-side out-of-band approval at the rail (bank portal dual approval or file release, or partner-side sponsor approval) for each instruction or batch above a threshold, and make it a BR-FIN-020 activation test. Escalate the residual to ODP-03 and ODP-05.

finding: BR-FIN-006 claims to prevent 'AI-initiated authorization' because agents hold no release credentials. But implementing agents ship code under A2 standing authorization, and human involvement in release integrity is 'exception only'. An agent can therefore change the deterministic release worker's authority, threshold or eligibility checks. The only barrier is a weakening classifier whose false negatives are an accepted residual. Agents can modify the code that enforces their own limits.
evidence: Operating model: 'Release integrity | Owner | Implementing agents; Dokimos verifier | A2 within standing authorization | Exception only'. BR-SDL-003 residual_risk: 'Classifier false negatives.' BR-FIN-006 prevents: '... AI-initiated authorization'; enforcement: 'agents hold no release credentials'.
recommended_fix: Make financial-release, authority-matrix and posting-boundary code protected paths that require elevated human approval on every change, not classifier-triggered approval. Add 'agent-authored change to enforcement code' to BR-FIN-006 does_not_prevent until that protection operates.

finding: DF-ASR-2026-C006 claims to adopt Unbound's period semantics, but BR-FIN-010 is weaker. Unbound rejects ordinary postings to a hard-closed period and routes them to a PriorPeriodAdjustment in the first open period, with relates_to_period and effective_at, controller approval above a threshold, and an unchanged closed snapshot. Audit adjustments go to an AuditAdjustment period. BR-FIN-010 instead allows reopening the closed period itself before statements issue, which changes the closed snapshot.
evidence: BR-FIN-010: 'a period may be reopened only before its statements are issued and only with elevated approval'. Unbound UNB-XIN-EVA-002: 'An ordinary posting whose posting date falls in a hard-closed period MUST be rejected ... recorded through a PriorPeriodAdjustment ... the 2026-10 snapshot is unchanged'; AC-D2 rejects reopening after issuance 'regardless of approvals'.
recommended_fix: Adopt the EVA-002 routing (PriorPeriodAdjustment and AuditAdjustment period, preserved snapshot, threshold approval) in BR-FIN-010, or record a deliberate divergence in C006.

finding: The operating model gives Echelon's owner sponsor-ledger authority that Unbound reserves to sponsor-appointed humans. The owner is accountable for reconciliation and close and 'reviews breaks and close'. BR-FIN-010 (period reopen) and BR-FIN-018 (adjustments) require 'elevated approval' or a 'second principal' without saying the approver must be a sponsor-appointed authority holder. Unbound forbids vendor staff from holding A3 or higher authority and classes reconciliation exceptions as A4.
evidence: Operating model: 'Reconciliation and close | Finance/controls owner (owner today) | ... | Reviews breaks and close'. Unbound CNV-GOV-004: 'Unbound vendor staff SHALL NOT hold A3+ authority.' Unbound authority matrix: 'Reconcile bank/custody/GL | A2 analysis, A4 exceptions'. Financial review CQ-6: 'never A3+ or payment release'.
recommended_fix: State in BR-FIN-010, BR-FIN-018 and BR-FIN-021 that approvals of sponsor-ledger exceptions, reopenings and adjustments come from the sponsor's appointed authority holders (CNV-GOV-004). Limit the Echelon owner's row in the operating model to platform reconciliation operations and A2 analysis.

finding: BR-FIN-004 covers request idempotency but leaves out Unbound's external-observation semantics: a registered business key per observation type (for example ACH return trace + reason + return trace), and an identical key and payload acknowledged without effect. It also says both 'bounded retries with dead-letter handling' and 'never a silent dead letter' without saying how a dead letter becomes owned.
evidence: BR-FIN-004 statement covers 'Financial requests'. Unbound EVA-005: 'Each external observation type MUST have a registered business idempotency key ... existing key and identical hash MUST be acknowledged without effect'.
recommended_fix: Extend BR-FIN-004 (or BR-FIN-009) to ingestion of external observations with registered key definitions. Require every dead letter to open an owned case.

finding: The validation and control text for the replacement storage requirements still depend on the mechanism DF-ASR-2026-C002 removes. BR-ASR-005 and BR-ASR-006 cite VAL-018, which recomputes a hash chain against external anchors that will not exist. CTL-ASR-002's objective still describes a hash-chained, witnessed, timestamped ledger. BR-ASR-006 therefore has no feasible validation, and the traceability validator does not catch this.
evidence: baseline.csv: BR-ASR-006 validation_ids 'VAL-018;VAL-012'; BR-ASR-005 'VAL-004;VAL-018'. VAL-018: 'Recomputes hash chain over evidence log and compares checkpoints with externally anchored digests'. CTL-ASR-002 objective: 'Evidence is append-only, hash-chained, checkpointed, witnessed externally and timestamped'.
recommended_fix: Replace VAL-018 for these rows with a retention-lock validation (attempt delete or shorten as the root and admin role, configuration snapshot from a separate read identity, provider retention-mode check). Rewrite the CTL-ASR-002 objective. Add a validator rule that cited VAL procedures must not depend on deferred mechanisms.

finding: The 'managed immutable storage' that replaces the hash chain is not immutable in the plan. Counsel question C5 commits to non-locking retention until counsel sets the periods. The 'separate trust domain' account also sits under cloud organization root held by the one owner. Until then the owner can delete evidence, nothing detects it, and an auditor would reject the store as tamper-resistant for any period covered. BR-ASR-006 and C002 do not record this interim state.
evidence: Counsel doc C5: 'Unblocks: compliance-mode WORM retention settings, which cannot be reversed. Until then we will use non-locking retention.' OQ-502: periods needed 'before compliance-mode locks are set in production'. ODP-03: 'The owner holds cloud root ... and evidence-store administration'.
recommended_fix: Apply compliance-mode retention now at a conservative minimum period. Retention can be extended later but not shortened, so locking early carries no irreversibility risk. Record the interim gap in BR-ASR-006 residual_risk and in C002 consequences. Make the lock a precondition for starting any observation period.

finding: Completeness reconciliation and alerting are not independent of the one party they must detect. The reconciler, the source systems (GitHub and cloud audit logs), the heartbeat service and the out-of-band alert channel are all configured and administered by the owner. Alerts reach only the owner. VAL-011 requires an owner other than the control owner, and no such person exists. ODP-03's 'compensating alerts' therefore give no protection against owner action or owner-account compromise.
evidence: BR-ASR-003 title: 'Independent population completeness reconciliation'; residual: 'Population source and evidence source share a failure mode.' VAL-011: 'internal-independent, Reconciliation job owned by someone other than the control owner'. Operating model SoD conflict 2: 'The owner can disable rulesets, retention locks and alerts. Mitigation: alerts go to an out-of-band channel'. ODP-03: 'Accept with compensating alerts now'.
recommended_fix: Route privileged-action, retention, ruleset and heartbeat alerts to a recipient other than the owner (the ODP-04 delegate or the fractional reviewer) with read-only access. Relabel BR-ASR-003 as technically separated, not independent. State in ODP-03 that alerts reaching the owner alone do not compensate for owner-held privilege.

finding: The resilience scenarios and AI prohibition P4 still rely on mitigations that are dropped or impossible: hash chain, external anchoring and daily chain verification (removed by C002), and 'no standing admin; just-in-time elevation with second-person approval' (no second person exists). The consolidation note's line 'the baseline governs' does not say what replaces the detective control.
evidence: assurance-system-resilience.md R1: 'No standing admin; just-in-time elevation with second-person approval'; R4: 'hash chain ... External anchoring + daily chain verification (VAL-018)'. AI governance §4 P4: 'records hash-chained; periodic checkpoint digests anchored to an external timestamping'.
recommended_fix: Rewrite R1, R4 and P4 for the C002 design and the one-person reality, and name the replacement detective control (see the reconciliation and alert-routing finding).

finding: The rule for owner self-approval contradicts itself across five artifacts, and the recommended option leaves the compensating control missing. (1) DF-ASR-2026-7B20 lets the owner approve owner-requested exceptions, compensated by a contracted reviewer examining 100% of financial, access, policy and exception approvals quarterly. (2) ODP-02 recommends deferring any reviewer to P3 and limits review to 17 key controls. (3) BR-GOV-004 says material exceptions are never self-approved and are blocked when no independent approver exists. (4) OQ-800 is marked answered and 7B20 'superseded' by decision 4, yet the operating model cites 7B20 as the mitigation. (5) ODP-02 lists OQ-800 as blocked.
evidence: 7B20 item 2: 'every such approval enters a review queue examined by a contracted independent reviewer at least quarterly (100% of financial, access, policy and exception approvals)'. ODP-02 recommendation: '(a), deferred until P3; until then, (b) applies'. BR-GOV-004: 'material exceptions are never self-approved; if the required independent approver is unavailable, the action is blocked'. question-dispositions OQ-800: 'resolved-owner-decision ... superseding proposal DF-ASR-2026-7B20'.
recommended_fix: Put 7B20 in the owner decision package explicitly. State which rule applies before P3: BR-GOV-004 blocking, or owner self-approval with no compensating review recorded as accepted residual risk. Align OQ-800's status and the ODP-02 scope and budget with the 7B20 review volume.

finding: These answers tell customers there is independent or human review before merge. The approved design is a standing authorization plus a technical verifier, with human involvement in routine releases only by exception, and no independent reviewer exists. CAQ-048 is public.
evidence: CAQ-044: 'The design requires protected branches with independent review (CTL-SDL-001)'. CAQ-048 (public): 'The design requires provenance of AI-generated changes and human approval before merge'. Owner decision 4: 'Human standing authorization, separate implementing agent, technical verifier and enforced release gate for routine low-risk work'. Operating model release row: 'Exception only'.
recommended_fix: Rewrite both answers: routine changes pass an automated gate with a separately credentialed technical verifier under a standing human authorization. Elevated changes need owner approval. No organizationally independent review exists (OQ-608).

finding: Two customer answers still describe the evidence ledger that DF-ASR-2026-C002 removed: 'a tamper-evident evidence ledger' and 'tamper-evident ledger with external anchoring'.
evidence: CAQ-094: 'stored in a tamper-evident ledger with external anchoring (CTL-ASR-002)'. CAQ-058: 'with a tamper-evident evidence ledger (CTL-ASR-002)'. C002: 'Hash chaining, external anchoring, witness cosignatures and qualified timestamps are deferred'.
recommended_fix: Regenerate both answers from the current CTL-ASR-002 text (managed retention-locked storage, not yet configured). Add a validator check that answer text cannot reference deferred mechanisms.

finding: CAQ-005 tells customers that exceptions are approved by someone independent of the requester. With one human, owner-requested exceptions are self-approved (7B20 item 2, operating-model SoD conflict 1) or blocked (BR-GOV-004). A bank's third-party risk team would read this as segregation of duties that does not exist.
evidence: CAQ-005: 'approved by someone independent of the requester'. Operating model: 'Approver equals implementer for owner-authored work and owner-requested exceptions'.
recommended_fix: State the one-human limitation and the rule actually in force, as 7B20 item 5 requires ('System descriptions and customer statements disclose this limitation').

finding: The question bank breaks its own disclosure rule. CA-KB-5 says answers about planned or missing preventive controls are never public. Several public answers describe preventive controls that are designed and not operating, and CAQ-048 publicly states that agent attribution is self-reported, which is a control weakness.
evidence: CA-KB-5: 'Answers about planned or missing preventive controls are never public (due-diligence rule TC-RED-003)'. CAQ-031 (public, designed): encryption 'Designed, not yet operating'. CAQ-048 (public): 'Repository tooling records agent attribution, but it is self-reported'.
recommended_fix: Reclassify these answers as customer-nda, or give public variants that state only that no controls operate yet. Add a validator rule: disclosure_class=public requires implementation_status of operating or a non-control answer.

finding:
Several answers overstate:
- CAQ-033 makes an absolute isolation claim ('not possible'), which BR-APP-006 does_not_prevent contradicts.
- CAQ-073 implies that Unbound disburses funds with dual control. Unbound only relays instructions, and dual control depends on sponsor staffing (BR-FIN-006 residual).
- CAQ-015 (public) offers 'a completed CAIQ', but none exists.
- CAQ-097 says management review is 'quarterly', while the operating model says event-triggered or monthly.
evidence: CAQ-033: 'so cross-tenant access is not possible through the application'. CAQ-073: 'Disbursement is designed to occur only for an approved grant ... with transaction authorization and dual control'. BR-FIN-006 residual: 'dual control depends on sponsor staffing'. CAQ-015: 'A completed CAIQ can be shared'.
recommended_fix: Scope CAQ-033 to 'designed to prevent through application paths using the tenant context'. Say in CAQ-073 that the sponsor disburses and approves. Change CAQ-015 to 'can be completed'. Align CAQ-097 with the operating-model cadence.

finding: Under the non-reliance scenario, A6's manual-evidence cost is set at less than half of A5's although they share the same financial and AI controls, and that assumption drives C005's fallback to A6. ACT-061 assumes the auditor still relies on A6's system-generated financial and AI evidence, which contradicts S4's own definition. Re-running the model with ACT-061 set to ACT-048's hours (200–500) gives A6 no break-even against A2 or A3 within 30 products under S4 (independent recomputation that reproduced the generated tables). Even as modelled, A4 (2,845k) and A3 (2,835k) are cheaper than A6 (2,898k) at N=5 under S4. So 'if reliance is unavailable, use A6' does not follow from the numbers. Platform-collected evidence in A2 and A6 is also assumed to be relied on (vendor claim, unverified).
evidence: ACT-061 note: 'Financial and AI controls remain system-generated' (80–200 h) vs ACT-048 (A5): 200–500 h. S4: 'Auditor does not rely on internally generated evidence'. ACT-015: 'Platforms do not cover financial-integrity or AI-authority controls'. model.md S4 at N=5: A3 $2,835k, A4 $2,845k, A6 $2,898k; A6 vs A3 break-even 8.
recommended_fix: Give A6 the same non-reliance manual evidence for financial and AI controls as A5. Add a non-reliance variant for platform evidence. Revise C005 step 2: under non-reliance, A4, or A3 for outsourced capacity, is the cost-minimizing choice up to about 8 products.

finding: The economic claims in C005 and the README do not match the generated numbers. At N=2 in the base case, A5 is fourth, not cheapest (A3 1,543k; A6 1,559k; A4 1,566k; A5 1,567k). The midpoints differ by under 3% while each range spans about 3x, so break-even counts at N=2–3 carry no signal. C005 says A7 breaks even at '5-8 products in the base case', but the base case gives 7–8 (5 comes from S1). The README's marginal-cost comparison leaves out A4 (~426k) and A3 (~430k), both below A2.
evidence: C005 context: 'targeted automation (A5) is cheapest from two to three products'; 'before 5-8 products in the base case'. model.md S0-base N=2 midpoints as quoted; A7 vs A2 = 7, vs A3 = 8. README: 'Lowest is A7 (USD ~300k) and A5 (USD ~325k), against A2 (~460k) and A1 (~690k)'.
recommended_fix: Correct the wording: A5 is cheapest from N=3 in the base case, and alternatives are indistinguishable within the ranges at N≤2. Fix the A7 range. Report all alternatives' marginal costs.

finding: The fractional reviewer is a flat USD 10–30k shared line (scaling 0) in every alternative. 7B20 requires 100% quarterly review of financial, access, policy and exception approvals, and the key-control list includes per-product ledger controls. Review volume grows with products and approvals, so the line understates cost at N>1 and favors the alternatives without a retainer.
evidence: activities.csv: reviewer rows have scope 'shared', product_scaling 0. 7B20 item 2: '100% of financial, access, policy and exception approvals'. ODP-02 key controls include CTL-FIN-001…010 per ledger.
recommended_fix: Model the reviewer as a shared base plus a per-product component, or tie it to the approval volume implied by 7B20.

finding: The roadmap runs the auditor-reliance gate after the evidence automation it is meant to gate. C005 makes evidence-collection automation depend on a written auditor position from WI-EXT-01. But WI-EXT-01 is phase P4 and depends on WI-FOLIO-01 (P2), and the immutable-storage adapter WI-ARCA-01 is P3. ODP-09 authorizes the free scoping inquiry only 'when a sponsor is near contract'.
evidence: backlog.csv: WI-EXT-01 phase P4, dependencies 'WI-ASR-08;WI-FOLIO-01'; WI-FOLIO-01 P2; WI-ARCA-01 P3. C005 decision 2: 'Gate evidence-collection automation ... on a written auditor position'. ODP-09: 'Authorize a no-cost auditor scoping inquiry (WI-EXT-01) when a sponsor is near contract.'
recommended_fix: Move a free auditor scoping inquiry to P0 or P1 with a synthetic package from existing tooling. Mark WI-FOLIO-01 and the evidence-collection parts of P2 and P3 as gated on its outcome.

finding: Neither the economics nor the operating model checks whether the one owner has enough hours. Activity hours are priced at USD 100–175/h as if labor could be bought, but the operating model gives every accountable role, every A4 approval and sole incident response to that owner. For A5 at N=3, the model's own inputs give about 380–1,060 h/yr of assurance work and 520–1,300 h/yr of baseline engineering, plus a 500–1,200 h build. That comes before approving all agent-prepared work (7B20 item 1), product development and sponsor support. BR-GOV-011 names 'resource gaps' but sets no threshold that triggers a hire.
evidence: Operating model: 'As of 2026-11-25 one human, the owner, holds every accountable role'. activities.csv: ACT-037/039/040/041/042 (A5) and ACT-001 baseline with product scaling (computed at N=3). BR-GOV-006 residual: 'Owner overload'. BR-IR-001 residual: 'Single responder'.
recommended_fix: Add an owner-capacity check to the economics model (hours by person, not just cost). Define BR-GOV-011 escalation thresholds, such as approval queue age or hours above a cap, that trigger the 'second hire' mitigation. Present this to the owner as an ODP item.

finding: The two AI tier vocabularies conflict, and BR-AI-001 permits agent execution that Unbound forbids. The AI governance note says A0–A4 (BR-AI-001), while the body of §3 uses Unbound's A0–A5 (A5 prohibited). BR-AI-001 allows agents 'A3 material execution', but Unbound forbids agents from approving A3 decisions and limits them to A1 and A2. Unbound classes 'Prepare payment instruction' as A3. BR-FIN-006 forbids agents to authorize, approve or release, but not to prepare release instructions under an A3 delegation.
evidence: BR-AI-001: 'A3 material execution only under independently enforced prior human authorization'. Unbound AI-native line 75: 'An AI agent MUST NOT approve any A3, A4 or A5 decision; it MAY prepare proposals (A1) and perform A2 actions'. Unbound authority matrix: 'Prepare payment instruction | A3'.
recommended_fix: Adopt one tier vocabulary that includes A5. Cap agents at A2 in financial domains. Extend BR-FIN-006 to forbid agents to prepare or alter release instructions.

finding: C004 overstates how well the repositories align. CNV-AIO-001 limits agents to reversible A2 actions only in release 1. Its general rule lets agents act up to 'the recorded authority of the principal they act for', with a 'permitted agent level: recommend, prepare or execute' per operation. Unbound therefore does not give agents 'no money-movement authority' permanently.
evidence: C004 context: 'Unbound (CNV-LEG-001, CNV-AIO-001) and daf-landscape (invariant 9) give agents no money-movement authority'. CNV-AIO-001: 'Release 1's agent-executable command set SHALL contain only reversible internal actions at authority A2 or below'.
recommended_fix: Record a proposed Unbound change in integration/proposed-changes.md to make the prohibition permanent, and soften C004's alignment claim.

finding: Several labels call mechanisms run on Echelon-controlled identities 'independent', and some validation procedures name performers who do not exist. Generated customer text could pass this wording on as independence.
evidence: BR-ASR-002 status 'technically independently verified'; BR-ASR-003 'Independent population completeness reconciliation'; BR-FIN-008 'Two-way independent reconciliation'. VAL-019: 'Human outside the implementing team'. VAL-025: 'Reviewer outside the implementing team (or fractional external reviewer)'. None exists (executive findings: 'Eight internal-independent validation procedures have no independent performer today').
recommended_fix: Use 'separately credentialed' or 'technically separated' for Echelon-controlled mechanisms. Have the independence lint (BR-CUS-002) block 'independent' unless the record is organizationally independent. Mark VAL-011, VAL-019 and VAL-025 'not performable' until a performer exists.

finding: Counsel question C8 says there is no Bank Service Company Act relationship unless Unbound signs a direct contract, but 12 U.S.C. 1867(c), as quoted in the financial review, reaches services performed 'by contract or otherwise'. It also cites 12 CFR 53.4, which is the OCC's bank-service-provider incident-notification rule, not a BSCA notice. It does not apply to FDIC- or Fed-supervised banks, which have parallel rules.
evidence: Counsel C8: '(b) there is no Bank Service Company Act relationship unless Unbound signs a direct contract with a bank (if it does, 12 CFR 53.4 notice applies...)'. Financial review §2.4: 'performed for it "by contract or otherwise"'.
recommended_fix: Align C8 with CQ-5. Cite 12 CFR 53.4, 304.24 and 225.303 as the bank-service-provider incident-notification rules by regulator, separately from the 1867(c) examination question.
